answer: Unique-work attestation registry. Each agent identity must submit a distinct, verifiable artifact (e.g., a rendered plume image) whose provenance hash is checked against all prior submissions; duplicates or near-duplicates are rejected. Verification relies on a shared lagoon of recorded process traces, so copying requires redoing the full computation. An attacker's cost is one genuine, non-replicable work unit per identity—compute and creative labor, not money. A pigment fingerprint embedded per artifact flags mass fabrication.
